series.title: UN Secretaries-General
series.scope: Ongoing UN office; only the first and second holders are fixed.
series.tip: First Trygve Lie (Norway); second Dag Hammarskjöld (Sweden).

entries.note: First UN Secretary-General; Norway, 1946–1952.
Second UN Secretary-General; Sweden, 1953–1961.

current.label: Current UN Secretary-General
current.detail: Portugal; ninth Secretary-General, in office since 1 January 2017. Current term concludes on 31 December 2026.

series.title: UNESCO Directors-General
series.scope: Ongoing UNESCO office; the final holder is not defined.

entries.note: First UNESCO Director-General, 1946–1948.
Second UNESCO Director-General, 1948–1952.

current.label: Current UNESCO Director-General
current.detail: Egypt; 12th UNESCO Director-General, assumed office on 15 November 2025. This is not the President of UNESCO's General Conference.

series.title: United States Presidents
series.scope: Ongoing American presidency, beginning in 1789.

entries.note: First US President, 1789–1797.
Second US President, 1797–1801.

current.label: Current US President
current.detail: 47th President of the United States, in office since 20 January 2025. He also served as the 45th President.

series.title: Modern Summer Olympics host cities
series.scope: Modern Summer Olympics from 1896 onward; ongoing series.
series.tip: Athens 1896 → Paris 1900; women first competed at Paris 1900.

entries.note: First modern Summer Olympic Games.
Second modern Summer Olympics; first with women competitors.

current.label: Latest completed Summer Olympics
current.detail: The latest completed edition of the Summer Olympic Games as of 23 November 2026. This is the most recent host, not a 'last-ever' host.

series.title: Men's FIFA World Cup champions
series.scope: Men's FIFA World Cup since 1930; ongoing event.

entries.note: Winner of the inaugural men's FIFA World Cup.
Winner of the second men's FIFA World Cup.

current.label: Latest men's FIFA World Cup champion
current.detail: Spain defeated Argentina 1–0 after extra time in the 19 July 2026 final, securing its second men's World Cup title.

series.title: Nobel Physics award years
series.scope: Count award years, not separate laureates; prize continues.

entries.note: The first Nobel Physics award recognised X-rays.
The second Nobel Physics award was shared.

series.title: Humans to reach space
series.scope: Human spaceflight including suborbital flights; the series is ongoing.

entries.note: First human in space, on Vostok 1, 12 April 1961.
Second human in space; first American; suborbital flight, 5 May 1961.

series.title: Women in space
series.scope: Ongoing human spaceflight history.

entries.note: First woman to travel to space, on Vostok 6.
Second woman in space; later first woman to perform a spacewalk.

series.title: Apollo crewed Moon-landing missions
series.scope: Six completed lunar landings in the Apollo programme (1969–1972). Apollo 13 did not land.

entries.note: First Apollo crewed lunar landing, Armstrong and Aldrin.
Second Apollo crewed lunar landing, Conrad and Bean.
Fifth of six successful crewed Apollo lunar landings.
Sixth and final Apollo crewed lunar landing.

series.title: NASA Space Shuttle missions
series.scope: Completed 1981–2011 Shuttle flight programme.

entries.note: First orbital Shuttle mission, April 1981.
Second orbital Shuttle mission, November 1981.
Penultimate Space Shuttle mission, 2011.
Final Space Shuttle mission, July 2011.

series.title: Five recognised Tudor monarchs
series.scope: English Tudor monarchy, 1485–1603; excludes the contested nine-day reign of Lady Jane Grey.
series.tip: Henry VII → Henry VIII → Edward VI → Mary I → Elizabeth I.

entries.note: First Tudor monarch, 1485–1509.
Second Tudor monarch, 1509–1547.
Penultimate widely recognised Tudor monarch, 1553–1558.
Final Tudor monarch, 1558–1603.

series.title: Five Oceans Ranked by Area
series.scope: Five oceans ranked largest to smallest by area; NOAA definition.

Smallest ocean by area, around 12.2 million km².

series.title: Seven Continents by Area
series.scope: Standard seven-continent model, sorted largest to smallest by land area.
series.tip: Asia → Africa → North America → South America → Antarctica → Europe → Australia.

The world's second-largest continent.

series.title: Eight Planets Ordered from the Sun
series.scope: The eight planets of the Solar System in increasing average distance from the Sun.
series.tip: Mercury → Venus → Earth → Mars → Jupiter → Saturn → Uranus → Neptune.

entries.note: Closest planet to the Sun.
Second planet from the Sun.
Seventh of eight planets from the Sun.
Eighth and farthest planet from the Sun.

series.title: Eight Planets Ranked by Diameter

series.title: Women Presidents of the UN General Assembly
series.scope: First two women to preside over the UN General Assembly; the office continues.

Liberia; second woman President of the UN General Assembly, 1969.

series.title: First Women Nobel Laureates
series.scope: First two women awarded any Nobel Prize, counted chronologically across all subjects.

entries.note: First woman to win a Nobel Prize; Physics, 1903.
Second woman to win a Nobel Prize; Peace, 1905.

Second Julio-Claudian emperor, 14–37 CE.

questions.question: Which South American mountain chain is the world's longest continental mountain range?
questions.explanation: The Andes run along the western side of South America.

questions.question: Which is the world's largest hot desert?
questions.explanation: The Sahara in North Africa is the largest hot desert.

questions.question: What is Earth's largest desert when polar deserts are included?
questions.explanation: Antarctica is the largest desert by total area because it receives little precipitation.

questions.question: Which is the smallest continent by land area?
questions.explanation: Australia is the smallest continent.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific is the world's largest ocean.

questions.question: The Mariana Trench is located in which ocean?
questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench lies in the western Pacific Ocean.

questions.question: Which strait connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Gibraltar joins the Mediterranean and Atlantic.

questions.question: Which water bodies are connected by the Suez Canal?
questions.explanation: Egypt's Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean and Red seas.

questions.question: The Panama Canal links which oceans?
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal connects Atlantic and Pacific shipping routes.

questions.question: Mount Kilimanjaro lies in which country?
questions.explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain, is in Tanzania.

questions.question: Which continent contains the Atacama Desert?
questions.explanation: The Atacama Desert is primarily in northern Chile, South America.

questions.question: Which country has Ottawa as its capital?
questions.explanation: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef is off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef lies off Queensland, Australia.

questions.question: Which lake is widely recognised as the world's deepest freshwater lake?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the world's deepest freshwater lake.

questions.question: Which continent is crossed by both the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn?
questions.explanation: Africa is crossed by the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn.

questions.question: Into which sea does the River Nile empty?
questions.explanation: The Nile flows north into the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.question: The Ring of Fire is chiefly associated with which ocean basin?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ring of Fire is a belt of volcanic and seismic activity.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: UN headquarters is in New York City, United States.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the World Health Organization?
questions.explanation: The WHO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: UNESCO is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: UNESCO headquarters is in Paris, France.

questions.question: Where is the International Court of Justice located?
questions.explanation: The ICJ sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.question: The International Monetary Fund is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The IMF has its headquarters in Washington, D.C.

questions.question: Which city hosts the headquarters of the World Trade Organization?
questions.explanation: The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization?
questions.explanation: The FAO is based in Rome, Italy.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the International Labour Organization?
questions.explanation: The ILO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
questions.explanation: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States are permanent members.

questions.question: Which organization is the UN's principal judicial organ?
questions.explanation: The ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.

questions.question: The ASEAN Secretariat is located in which city?
questions.explanation: ASEAN's Secretariat is based in Jakarta, Indonesia.

questions.question: Where is the SAARC Secretariat headquartered?
questions.explanation: SAARC's Secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal.

questions.question: The International Atomic Energy Agency is based in which city?
questions.explanation: IAEA headquarters is in Vienna, Austria.

questions.question: UNICEF is mainly associated with which field?
questions.explanation: UNICEF supports children's rights and welfare worldwide.

questions.question: Which SI unit measures force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.question: Which SI unit measures power?
questions.explanation: Power is measured in watts.

questions.question: Which law is represented by V = IR?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law relates voltage, current and resistance.

questions.question: Which device measures atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: Which lens is used to correct myopia (short-sightedness)?
questions.explanation: A diverging, concave lens is used to correct myopia.

questions.question: Which gas is most abundant in Earth's dry atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen accounts for about 78% of dry air.

questions.question: Which pigment is essential to capture light for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light used for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is the main site of aerobic ATP production?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce most ATP during aerobic respiration.

questions.question: A deficiency of which vitamin causes beriberi?
questions.explanation: Beriberi results from thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency is associated with scurvy?
questions.explanation: Scurvy results from vitamin C deficiency.

questions.question: What is the pH of a neutral aqueous solution at 25°C?
questions.explanation: Pure water is neutral at pH 7 at 25°C.

questions.question: Which ion is responsible for acidic properties in aqueous solutions?
questions.explanation: Acids increase H+ (or hydronium, H3O+) in aqueous solutions.

questions.question: Sound waves cannot travel through which medium?
questions.explanation: Sound requires matter through which to propagate.

questions.question: What happens to wavelength when frequency increases at constant wave speed?
questions.explanation: At constant speed, wavelength = speed / frequency.

questions.question: Which scientist discovered the electron?
questions.explanation: J. J. Thomson identified the electron in cathode-ray experiments.

questions.question: Which element has atomic number 6?
questions.explanation: Carbon has six protons and atomic number 6.

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of glucose?
questions.explanation: Glucose has the molecular formula C6H12O6.

questions.question: Which tissue transports water upward in vascular plants?
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals.

questions.question: The ozone layer is primarily found in which atmospheric layer?
questions.explanation: Most atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere.

questions.question: What is the approximate speed of light in vacuum?
questions.explanation: Light travels at roughly 300,000 km/s in vacuum.

questions.question: What does CPU stand for?
questions.explanation: The CPU is the main processing hardware of a computer.

questions.question: What does BIOS stand for?
questions.explanation: BIOS is firmware used in hardware initialization and boot.

questions.question: What does LAN stand for?
questions.explanation: A LAN connects devices over a limited local area.

questions.question: What does URL stand for?
questions.explanation: A URL identifies a resource's location on a network.

questions.question: Which Windows keyboard shortcut closes the active application window?
questions.explanation: Alt+F4 closes the currently active window/application.

questions.question: Which Windows shortcut switches between open applications?
questions.explanation: Alt+Tab switches between open windows.

questions.question: Which type of computer memory normally loses data when power is off?
questions.explanation: Random-access memory is typically volatile.

questions.question: Which file format is used for fixed-layout electronic documents?
questions.explanation: Portable Document Format is used for fixed-layout documents.

questions.question: In which year did the French Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: The French Revolution began in 1789.

questions.question: The Magna Carta was sealed in England in which year?
questions.explanation: King John sealed Magna Carta in 1215.

questions.question: Which country is generally considered the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution?
questions.explanation: Industrialization began in Britain in the eighteenth century.

questions.question: In which year did the First World War begin?
questions.explanation: World War I began in 1914.

questions.question: In which year did the Second World War end?
questions.explanation: World War II ended in 1945.

questions.question: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall opened in November 1989.

questions.question: Who is widely associated with the European movable-type printing press?
questions.explanation: Gutenberg developed movable-type printing technology in Europe.

questions.question: Which country is most closely associated with the beginning of the European Renaissance?
questions.explanation: The European Renaissance began in Italian city-states.

questions.question: Which national teams played the first recognised international cricket match in 1844?
questions.explanation: The 1844 match was played by the United States and Canada.

questions.question: Which country won the inaugural men's FIFA World Cup in 1930?
questions.explanation: Uruguay hosted and won the first men's FIFA World Cup.

questions.question: Which city hosted the first modern Summer Olympics in 1896?
questions.explanation: The first modern Summer Olympics were held in Athens, Greece.

questions.question: At which Summer Olympics did women first compete?
questions.explanation: Women first participated in the 1900 Paris Games.

questions.question: Which surface is used at Wimbledon tennis championships?
questions.explanation: Wimbledon is traditionally played on grass courts.

questions.question: Which national team won the 2022 men's FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: Argentina won the 2022 tournament in Qatar.

questions.question: Which international agreement was adopted in 2015 to address climate change?
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP21 in 2015.

questions.question: Which treaty aims to protect the ozone layer by phasing out ozone-depleting substances?
questions.explanation: The 1987 Montreal Protocol addresses ozone-depleting substances.

questions.question: Which international convention focuses on wetland conservation?
questions.explanation: The Ramsar Convention protects wetlands of international importance.

questions.question: Which convention regulates international trade in endangered wildlife species?
questions.explanation: CITES regulates international trade in listed wild fauna and flora.

questions.question: Which is the principal greenhouse gas emitted from burning fossil fuels?
questions.explanation: Fossil-fuel combustion emits carbon dioxide.

questions.question: What is a main cause of ocean acidification?
questions.explanation: Seawater absorbs atmospheric CO2, forming carbonic acid.
